title: Minimum Non-Zero Product
description: Given a positive integer `p`, consider the array `nums = [1, 2, ..., 2^p - 1]` containing every positive `p`-bit integer. In one operation you may choose two elements of `nums` and swap their bits at any single bit position. Return the minimum possible non-zero product of all elements of `nums` after any number of operations, modulo `10^9 + 7`.
hints: Swapping bits preserves the sum of the two chosen numbers while minimizing their product when pushed as far apart as possible (while remaining >= 1).
Pair every complementary pair `(x, (2^p - 1) - x)` into `(1, 2^p - 2)`, leaving one unpaired `2^p - 1`; the minimum product is `(2^p - 1) * (2^p - 2)^(2^(p - 1) - 1) mod (10^9 + 7)`.

examples.explanation: For p = 1, nums = [1] and the product is 1.
For p = 2, nums = [1, 2, 3] already minimizes the non-zero product at 1 * 2 * 3 = 6.
For p = 3, pairing gives [1, 1, 1, 6, 6, 6, 7], whose product is 6^3 * 7 = 1512.
